The Treasurer. The Commissioner of the Revenue sets the assessment, and the bill is addressed to the January 1 owner of record.

No. Norton is an independent city within the county's borders but separate from it, so take Norton questions to the city.

Rates and due dates

Nelson County taxes real estate at $0.56 per $100 of assessed value. Payment comes in two installments. Spring bills go in the mail May 1 with a June 5 deadline, and fall bills go out October 1 with a December 5 deadline. A countywide reassessment took effect January 1, 2026, so phone the Commissioner's office to check the rate on your own bill before quoting it to a buyer.

Real estate and personal property tax can be paid online at officialpayments.com using a credit card plus either the bill number or the tax map number. The site adds a convenience fee that scales with the payment. With only two bills a year, a missed December 5 deadline leaves an open balance that a title company will find when it asks for a payoff.

Who to call

Nelson County splits assessment from collection, as most Virginia localities do. One office decides what your property is worth: the Commissioner of the Revenue. A different one, the Treasurer, mails bills and accepts money. Questions about value go to the Commissioner. Questions about paying or getting a payoff go to the Treasurer.

  • Commissioner of the Revenue: 84 Courthouse Square, P.O. Box 246, Lovingston, VA 22949, phone 434-263-7070.
  • County Administrator, including Board of Equalization scheduling: 84 Courthouse Square, phone 434-263-7000. The Board's appointment line is 434-263-7003.
  • Reassessment office: 800-213-7314, staffed by the appraisal firm the county hired for the project.

Lovingston is the county seat. The Clerk of the Circuit Court's office can tell you about recording fees and forms ahead of closing day.

The 2026 reassessment

Nelson County reassessed every property effective January 1, 2026, and the next full reappraisal follows a four year schedule. Wampler-Eanes Appraisal Group did the field work with the Commissioner's office. Va. Code 58.1-3252 sets the default at four years, or three if the board votes for it, while a county with 50,000 or fewer residents may stretch the gap to five or six years.

Appraisers visited properties starting in fall 2024. They carried photo IDs, put magnetic signs on their vehicles, and took exterior photos and measurements. Notices of proposed values were expected in November 2025.

Exterior photos say nothing about the rooms inside. If your kitchen is torn out, your roof leaks or a floor is unfinished, ask what the county's record says about your parcel. Fixing the record before you list heads off a dispute with a buyer.

How to appeal your assessment

Owners who think a value is out of line with similar properties, or above what the house would sell for, take the case to the Board of Equalization. The board may raise the figure, cut it or affirm it. The county's public notice cites Va. Code 58.1-3378 and 58.1-3379.

  • Where: the Bridge Conference Room of the Lovingston courthouse.
  • Appointments: booked by calling 434-263-7003, scheduled every 30 minutes.
  • Burden: the county's number is presumed correct, so you need a preponderance of evidence showing non-uniformity or a value above the market.

The board sits after a reassessment, not every year. Ring the appointment line to find out if a session is open and when applications close. Collect nearby comparable sales, photos of defects, and any appraisal or contractor estimate you hold. Evidence about your own house beats general complaints about the rate.

Nelson County is rural. The 2020 population was 14,775, and no city or incorporated town sits inside the county lines. Of the homes people live in, 78.7 percent were owner occupied. Listings range from mountain cabins to farm parcels to family houses, and tax and road access questions differ for each.

Creek valleys in the county can fill quickly, and Hurricane Camille caused deadly flash floods here in 1969. If your house is close to a stream, pull together whatever flood or drainage records you have before listing, since buyers will ask. Check the parcel against the county or the FEMA map before you describe its flood status.

Selling with taxes owed

Real estate tax outranks every other lien under Va. Code 58.1-3340. At closing, the buyer or a foreclosure trustee pays it out of the proceeds, along with penalty and interest. Once paid, the Treasurer lifts the lien. How the year's tax is split between seller and buyer is a matter of contract, so write down who covers the current half.

Splitting a parcel off a bigger tract changes the math: the tax follows the portion of the price. A low price may lead the Commissioner to request an appraisal. If you sell five acres from a farm, the whole tract's taxes will come up at closing.

A separate grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 comes from Va. Code 58.1-802. Sellers owe it by default, though the parties can agree differently, and the clerk of court takes it when recording the deed.

For a value dispute, add photographs, repair quotes and prices from comparable sales nearby. Staff can say whether a fix is possible today or must wait for an appeal session. Note the date and who helped you.

Steps before you close

Four steps keep tax from stalling a sale. Request a written payoff from the Treasurer, with penalty and interest included. Look at the spring and fall bills to see which is paid. Warn the title company about any parcel split so the tract rule gets applied. Then read the contract's proration line and confirm it matches your plan.

Timing matters on a rural sale. Ask for the payoff early, because a parcel with several tax map numbers may need a separate figure for each. If the buyer is a lender-financed purchaser, the lender will want proof that taxes are current, and the title company usually collects that from the Treasurer. Cleaning up a balance before you list means one fewer item on the closing checklist and a faster path to a signed contract.

When the balance is big or repairs are beyond your budget, an as-is cash sale can pay the tax from proceeds on closing day. You skip repairs, showings and a lender's appraisal, but you still want the payoff letter and a careful look at the settlement statement.

When are Nelson County real estate taxes due?

Two payments: June 5 for the May 1 mailing, and December 5 for the October 1 mailing.

Who handles assessments in Nelson County?

The Commissioner of the Revenue, at 84 Courthouse Square in Lovingston, phone 434-263-7070.

Can I appeal a Nelson County reassessment?

Yes, in front of the Board of Equalization, which meets after a reassessment. Call 434-263-7003 about sessions and appointment times.

Can I sell Nelson County land with taxes owed?

Yes. The tax lien is settled from your proceeds, and a partial sale of a tract is prorated by price. Get a payoff from the Treasurer first.

A county with no towns, and Fredericksburg addresses

With a rural third of residents, some owners hold bigger parcels away from the busy corridor. Tell buyers early if the property has a private well or septic system, since testing takes time to schedule.

The county had 34,435 people in 1980, so most building happened since then and many houses are fairly new. State your own home's age and updates plainly. Interstate 95 is the main route, and commuters will ask how close you are to it.

Buyers who commute want to know how the house connects to the highways. Along with Interstate 95, the county is served by U.S. 1, U.S. 17 and U.S. 522 and by State Routes 2, 3 and 208. On the southern side, Lake Anna and Lake Anna State Park are well-known draws, and the North Anna River forms part of that border.

Four major Civil War battles took place here: Chancellorsville, the Wilderness, Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania Court House. The Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania National Military Park reaches into the county, and some properties appear on the National Register of Historic Places.

An older house, or one near battlefield land, deserves a call to county planning before you list: does any overlay, easement or review apply? Get the answer in writing.

How to appeal your assessment

First, ask the assessing office to take another look at your value. Still unhappy? File with the Board of Equalization. The assessor's figure starts out presumed correct, which means you must demonstrate the home is worth less than the assessment or that values were applied unevenly.

  • You carry the burden, and the standard is a preponderance of the evidence.
  • Sales made through the December 31 ahead of the assessment's effective date may be considered.
  • A study released after that December 31 cannot be used.
  • To keep the load fair among owners, the board may move a value up or down.

Clerical and factual errors follow another track. If the commissioner erred, or a factual mistake crept into a general reassessment, apply for a correction. The window is three years after the tax year ends or one year after the assessment, whichever ends later. Local filing dates vary, so ask the county which one applies.

Selling a house that was inherited

An inherited house with tax behind is common here, and it is manageable. Start by finding out who has legal authority to sell. If a will names someone, that person signs. If not, the heirs claim ownership by intestacy, and either route lets them ask the treasurer to pause a tax sale while a sale of the house is arranged.

Next, get a payoff from the treasurer, including penalty and interest. Then compare the number with the likely price. Closing pays the tax from the proceeds and clears the lien. A county, with no incorporated towns or cities inside it. Spotsylvania Courthouse is the seat. Fredericksburg is a separate city along its northeastern edge.

Mail routing, not city limits, explains it. County offices still assess and bill the property. The Commissioner of the Revenue can confirm for your parcel.

Generally until December 31 after the second anniversary of the due date. Condemned, derelict or blighted property can be sold after one year, and so can a house assessed at $100,000 or less, with a court finding.

Yes. Request an assessor review, then take it to the Board of Equalization and show the value exceeds market value or was not uniform. The county can give you its deadline.

Miss a deadline and the penalty is 10 percent of what you owe. Interest of 10 percent a year then builds on the tax and the penalty together. For the December bill it begins December 6 and is added on the first of every month after, citing Code of Virginia 58.1-3916.

Paying by mail works only when the envelope has a Post Office postmark dated on or before the deadline. A postage meter imprint is not accepted in its place.

Call the county Treasurer for balances and due dates, and the county's real estate office for values. Ask for the balance in writing.

What caused the 2011 earthquake damage in Louisa County?

Can a Louisa County tax penalty be waived after a death?

Virginia law presumes the taxpayer was not at fault if payment comes within 30 days of the due date after a death or medical impairment. A fiduciary has 120 days after qualifying.
